To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

(1) BIX01294 enhances TMZ-induced cytotoxicity in human glioma cells and in glioma stem-like cell cultures; (2) BIX012394 increases the expression of apoptosis-related genes and proteins in TMZ-treated cells; (3) BIX012494 does not influence the methylation of MGMT and NANOG gene promoters; and (4) the additive effect of BIX012494 and TMZ is stronger in LN18 than in U251 cells.
pre- and post-treatment of glioma cells with BIX01254, the G9a methyltransferase inhibitor, sensitize cells to temozolomide, a first line drug used in treatment of glioblastoma patients.
the combination of BIX01294 with TMZ sensitizes glioma cells to the drug and restores their apoptosis competence.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the possibility of epigenetically modifying glioma cells to enhance their response to TMZ.
the possibility of reprogramming of glioma cells by the inhibitor of histone methylation to increase sensitivity to chemotherapy.
the possibility of epigenetics-based reprogramming of glioma cells, which may be useful in the treatment of GBM patients.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that

BIX01294 sensitizes glioma cells to temozolomide by increasing apoptosis and autophagy and by reprogramming cells to a more differentiated phenotype, which could have therapeutic potential for the treatment of GBM.
BIX01294 sensitizes LN18 cells to TMZ and that this effect is associated with the induction of autophagy.
pre-treatment with Bix01294 increases the cytotoxic effect on glioma stem cells, but not on the differentiated cells, which may be a promising therapeutic approach in glioblastoma treatment.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
BIX01294 sensitizes glioma cells to the effect of TMZ by increasing the levels of apoptosis and autophagy.
BIX01294 is a good candidate for further clinical trials.
BIX01294 sensitizes human glioma cells to temozolomide, and this effect is not associated with modulation in expression of stemness markers.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the combination of TMZ and BIX01294 is a promising approach to increase sensitivity to the chemotherapy in glioblastoma patients.
G9a inhibitor BIX01294 sensitizes glioma cells to the standard chemotherapeutic agent TMZ and may be considered for further preclinical studies and clinical trials.
BIX01294 is a promising drug to sensitize GBM to TMZ and to restore apoptosis in glioma cells.
